steps.claim: The source has one persistent classical memory across H/CC/R/L, and indirect-call candidates belong to the device closure. Calling a helper that increments global g twice must preserve its first increment. The documented approved interim may instead stop with exit125 and a promised/pending diagnostic before silently resetting state.
steps.by: clause:dialect §17.1, "There is one classical memory, shared by H, CC, R and the entry state of every L invocation"; clause:dialect §14.2, "The device closure includes every candidate"; docs/quality.md, Contracts and remaining mechanics, approved native adapter interim.

steps.claim: sharesGlobalState recursively visits functions found among IR operands, but an integer entry parameter converted to a function pointer has no helper Function operand. Analysis::candidates nevertheless includes the address-taken, type-compatible helper, and Entry::lowerCall emits a static call to its global-mutating CC body. Consequently top is scanned as unshared even though its generated device closure accesses mutable g.

On LLVM18 and LLVM23, use the default production budget and the same integer argument 4198720, the real source-native helper address. A validated comparison-layout file maps that address to the emitted helper; structure correspondence and host bitcode verification both pass. Source-native calls print "1 2 host_global=2"; generated host calls exit0, print "1 1 host_global=0", and produce no diagnostic. This also reproduces without a supplied layout using its standalone function address.

The native launch adapter silently violates the shared-memory result and bypasses its approved fail-loud interim. This is S0 contract divergence, with the prior direct-call ordering fix only partially covering the dependency problem; it does not establish a defect in the emitted device helper rows themselves.

sol.problem: S0: an indirect entry can invoke a mutable-global helper without triggering the shared-global guard. The host adapter creates and unloads a fresh program per call, discarding the device global and leaving the host global unchanged. Both supported majors silently produce the wrong observable values. The exact fixture and same-input, real-address comparison-layout reproduction are retained under tmp-sol.
sol.fix: In src/Production.cpp::sharesGlobalState and replaceHostEntries, compute dependencies over the same complete direct/indirect candidate closure used by Entry::lowerCall, while all original entry/helper bodies still exist; pass Analysis or preserve its reachable-function/global sets before body replacement. Dialect §17.1 says "There is one classical memory, shared by H, CC, R and the entry state of every L invocation" and §14.2 says "The device closure includes every candidate". Under the already-approved interim in docs/quality.md, every affected indirect entry must emit the existing promised/pending diagnostic containing bp-acm and b-dialect-spec-6u6, exit125 and emit no result output; full sharing, when implemented, must instead preserve 1 2 host_global=2. Add a regression in tests/review_regressions.py::global_cases with @g=global i32 0, an address-taken helper that loads g/adds1/stores/returns it, @keep=constant ptr @helper, and a marked top(i64 %fn) that inttoptr-casts %fn and calls it. Use a real resolved comparison map, pass the helper address for both calls, and use the default budget 1048576,1048576,65536,256,65536. Assert the source-native baseline and the interim generated-host exit/output/diagnostic on LLVM18/23 and in both helper/top orders. The current code exits0 with 1 1 host_global=0, so this test is red now. No spec change is needed.

steps.by: clause:DLT-16.3 ("a block created by a compare tree in block i ... in creation order"); clause:DLT-16.4 ("Y is a new block"); clause:ISA-3.6

steps.claim: The extracted lowerCall resets unsigned serial=0 for each indirect call. Two two-candidate calls in the same block both emit ^b0.s1. The switch and indirectbr paths also allocate from the same source-block name prefix independently.

The saved fixture defines one(x)=x+1, two(x)=x+2, selects their pointers, and calls the selected pointer twice in one block. LLVM 18 and 23 both lower successfully; bennett-isa-ref check and run-oracle both exit 1 with §3.6: duplicate block label. Expected with input 1,7 is payload 9, and with 0,7 payload 11, code 0 at budget 100,0,256,8.

A well-formed supported indirect-call composition produces an ill-formed object instead of the specified computation, an S0 lowering defect. This is inherited in the extracted code, not evidence of a newly introduced regression.

codex.problem: S0: compare-tree label numbering is call-local instead of source-block-local. The checked and executed object is rejected before either valid source path can run. The same reset is present in base 5a092cd; the current refactored Scalar::lowerCall still carries it.
codex.fix: Change src/Scalar.cpp Scalar::lowerCall and the switch/indirectbr emission in Scalar::body to share a monotonically increasing compare-block counter for each original BasicBlock. Dialect §16.3 requires "a block created by a compare tree in block i ... in creation order" and §16.4 requires "Y is a new block". Do not merely add the call ordinal to .s labels, which would change canonical naming. Add tmp-codex/two-calls.ll as a permanent scalar regression: on LLVM 18 and 23 compilation and ISA check must succeed; run-oracle ref --input 1,7 --budget 100,0,256,8 must return code 0/payload 9 and --input 0,7 must return code 0/payload 11. Add an indirect-call-followed-by-switch variant to prove the counter is shared across producers.

steps.claim: An indirect pointer that names a function without bitcode produces F(4) when reached; the compiler must still retain and execute the valid alternatives.
steps.by: clause:DLT-14.2 ("No match ... of a function without bitcode ... F(4) FAULT_UB_TRAP")

steps.claim: collectScalarFunction skips declarations, while Scalar::lowerCall retains those declarations in its candidate list and unconditionally evaluates functions.at(sorted[k]) for every leaf.

The saved valid LLVM fixture selects @one or declared @missing, supplies distinct comparison addresses through function metadata, and makes one indirect call. Both LLVM verifiers accept it. Both plugins abort with SIGABRT and std::out_of_range / map::at, even when the runtime selector would choose @one.

The required runtime fault alternative has become an unconditional compiler abort, preventing the valid branch too; this is S0. The same unchecked lookup exists at the base commit, so it is not labelled a new regression.

codex.problem: S0: a declaration in an indirect-call candidate set is absent from the lproc map but is indexed as if it had a definition. Compiler process termination replaces a defined fault outcome and also rejects inputs that choose the fully linked alternative.
codex.fix: Change src/Scalar.cpp Scalar::lowerCall together with collectScalarFunction as needed so a candidate with no definition selects the §14.2 fault-4 outcome, never functions.at on a missing entry. The controlling text is §14.2: "of a function without bitcode ... F(4) FAULT_UB_TRAP". Preserve all defined candidates and canonical compare-tree ordering.
